author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: During an interstellar war Earth cannot win, a drug that unsticks its users in time collides with a doctor's private crisis over whether to save a wife who has destroyed herself on it.
page_summary:
Earth is bound to a losing alliance in a war between two alien powers, and a new drug, JJ-180, is loose — instantly addictive and capable of throwing users backward and forward in time, into pasts and futures that may be alterable. Dr. Eric Sweetscent, artiforg surgeon to Earth's aging dictator Gino Molinari, is caught between the planetary crisis and his marriage to Kathy, who is disintegrating under the drug's effects.

The novel fuses PKD's drug and time obsessions into a single mechanism: an addiction that is also time travel, where the damage to a life and the damage to history run on the same track. Beneath the interstellar plot sits an intimate ethical question the book refuses to make easy — whether Eric owes loyalty to a wife who has ruined herself, a question posed, in the end, to a taxicab. Published in the mid-1960s, it turns the era's political dread inward, toward marriage, obligation, and the burden of a foreknowledge that may change nothing.
